verses.1: The Pharisees and some scribes came to him from Jerusalem,
verses.2: and they saw some of his disciples eating with unwashed hands—that is, with common hands.
verses.3: For the Pharisees and all the Jews never eat without washing their hands, holding to the tradition of the elders,
verses.4: and after returning from the marketplace they do not eat unless they purify themselves. And there are many other traditions they have held to—washings of cups, jugs, and copper vessels.
verses.5: So the Pharisees and scribes asked him, "Why do your disciples not live according to the tradition of the elders, but eat with common hands?"
verses.6: He said to them, "Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as it is written: 'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me;'
verses.7: 'they worship me in vain, teaching as doctrines human commandments.'
verses.8: You set aside the commandment of God in order to hold to human traditions."
verses.9: And he said to them, "You nullify the word of God through your tradition that you hand down;
verses.10: for Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother shall die;'
verses.11: but you say, 'If a man says to his father or his mother, "Whatever you might have received from me is Corban"—
verses.12: then you no longer let them do anything for their father or mother,
verses.13: making void the word of God through your tradition that you have handed down. And you do many such things like this."
verses.14: Again he called the crowd to him and said to them, "All of you, listen to me and understand.
verses.15: Nothing that enters from outside a person can defile them; it is the things coming out from a person that defile them."
verses.17: When he had entered a house, leaving the crowd behind, his disciples asked him about the parable.
verses.18: He said to them, "Are you so dull as well? Do you not understand that everything that enters from outside into a person cannot defile them,
verses.19: because it doesn't go into the heart but into the stomach, and then goes out into the sewer?" (Thus he declared all foods clean.)
verses.20: He said, "What comes out of a person is what defiles them;
verses.21: for from within, out of the heart of people, evil thoughts come: sexual immorality, theft, murder,
verses.22: adultery, greed, malice, deceit, sensuality, envy, slander, pride, foolishness;
verses.23: all these evil things come from within and defile a person."
verses.24: Then he left there and went to the district of Tyre. Entering a house, he did not want anyone to know he was there, but he could not remain hidden.
verses.25: Immediately a woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit heard about him. She came and fell at his feet.
verses.26: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by birth. She begged him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
verses.27: He said to her, "Let the children be fed first, for it is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
verses.28: But she answered him and said, "Lord, even the little dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs."
verses.29: Then he said to her, "Because of this answer, go. The demon has left your daughter."
verses.30: When she returned home, she found the child lying on the bed, and the demon had gone.
verses.31: Again he went out from the district of Tyre and passed through Sidon toward the Sea of Galilee, in the region of the Decapolis.
verses.32: They brought to him a deaf and mute man, and they begged him to lay his hand on him.
verses.33: Taking him aside from the crowd by himself, he put his fingers into the man's ears and touched his tongue with his spit,
verses.34: then looked up to heaven and sighed, and said to him, "Ephphatha," which means, "Be opened."
verses.35: Immediately his ears were opened and his tongue was loosed, and he began to speak clearly.
verses.36: And he told them not to tell anyone, but the more he told them, the more they proclaimed it.
verses.37: They were greatly amazed and said, "He has done all things well. He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak."

notes:
Notes
- v. 19: The parenthetical "Thus he declared all foods clean" is an interpretive rendering of the effect of Jesus' argument, though the Greek does not use such a phrase directly.
- v. 27: "dogs" is a culturally charged term; "little dogs" is a softened version appropriate to the context of a respectful reply.
- v. 35: "Ephphatha" is transliterated and followed by an explanation, as per the narrative's intent.
raw:
[1] The Pharisees and some scribes came to him from Jerusalem,
[2] and they saw some of his disciples eating with unwashed hands—that is, with common hands.
[3] For the Pharisees and all the Jews never eat without washing their hands, holding to the tradition of the elders,
[4] and after returning from the marketplace they do not eat unless they purify themselves. And there are many other traditions they have held to—washings of cups, jugs, and copper vessels.
[5] So the Pharisees and scribes asked him, "Why do your disciples not live according to the tradition of the elders, but eat with common hands?"
[6] He said to them, "Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as it is written: 'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me;'
[7] 'they worship me in vain, teaching as doctrines human commandments.'
[8] You set aside the commandment of God in order to hold to human traditions."
[9] And he said to them, "You nullify the word of God through your tradition that you hand down;
[10] for Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and 'Whoever speaks evil of father or mother shall die;'
[11] but you say, 'If a man says to his father or his mother, "Whatever you might have received from me is Corban"—
[12] then you no longer let them do anything for their father or mother,
[13] making void the word of God through your tradition that you have handed down. And you do many such things like this."
[14] Again he called the crowd to him and said to them, "All of you, listen to me and understand.
[15] Nothing that enters from outside a person can defile them; it is the things coming out from a person that defile them."
[17] When he had entered a house, leaving the crowd behind, his disciples asked him about the parable.
[18] He said to them, "Are you so dull as well? Do you not understand that everything that enters from outside into a person cannot defile them,
[19] because it doesn't go into the heart but into the stomach, and then goes out into the sewer?" (Thus he declared all foods clean.)
[20] He said, "What comes out of a person is what defiles them;
[21] for from within, out of the heart of people, evil thoughts come: sexual immorality, theft, murder,
[22] adultery, greed, malice, deceit, sensuality, envy, slander, pride, foolishness;
[23] all these evil things come from within and defile a person."
[24] Then he left there and went to the district of Tyre. Entering a house, he did not want anyone to know he was there, but he could not remain hidden.
[25] Immediately a woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit heard about him. She came and fell at his feet.
[26] The woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by birth. She begged him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
[27] He said to her, "Let the children be fed first, for it is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."
[28] But she answered him and said, "Lord, even the little dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs."
[29] Then he said to her, "Because of this answer, go. The demon has left your daughter."
[30] When she returned home, she found the child lying on the bed, and the demon had gone.
[31] Again he went out from the district of Tyre and passed through Sidon toward the Sea of Galilee, in the region of the Decapolis.
[32] They brought to him a deaf and mute man, and they begged him to lay his hand on him.
[33] Taking him aside from the crowd by himself, he put his fingers into the man's ears and touched his tongue with his spit,
[34] then looked up to heaven and sighed, and said to him, "Ephphatha," which means, "Be opened."
[35] Immediately his ears were opened and his tongue was loosed, and he began to speak clearly.
[36] And he told them not to tell anyone, but the more he told them, the more they proclaimed it.
[37] They were greatly amazed and said, "He has done all things well. He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak."
